articles.title: Pellegrini: "Faltan un par de retoques, pero el plantel va por el camino correcto"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Betis valora muy positivamente el triunfo de su equipo en Mestalla por 0-1
articles.summary: El técnico del Betis valora muy positivamente el triunfo de su equipo en Mestalla por 0-1
articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini, se mostró muy satisfecho con el rendimiento de su equipo, rotaciones incluidas, en su victoria por 0-1 en Mestalla frente al Valencia. Un golazo de Pablo García en los minutos finales del partido le dio a los verdiblancos su segundo triunfo de la temporada para firmar un pleno de seis puntos de seis posibles que sitúan a los andaluces en la zona alta de la clasificación... empatados con su eterno rival, el Sevilla. Valoración del triunfo: "La verdad que tres puntos muy importantes ante un rival difícil, además jugando de visita. Creo que fue un partido muy disputado por los dos equipos, muy cerrado con pocas ocasiones, pero creo que al final fuimos justo ganadores". Lo que más destaca de su equipo: "Bueno, primero la concentración defensiva. Quizás muchos tuvieran sorpresa que se cambiara toda la línea de cuatro, pero venimos de una pretemporada recién terminada. Tenemos que jugar ocho partidos en 27 días, en 26 días, así que no sentía que era un riesgo porque le había visto de rendimiento, que al final es lo que indica cuáles son los titulares, a los ocho defensores durante toda la pretemporada. Así que muy contento por haber podido ocupar el plantel y estamos todos compenetrados en sacar los resultados. Después creo que el funcionamiento del equipo, manteniendo otra vez la portería en blanco de todo el equipo, comprometido en la recuperación y muy ordenado, creo que nos hizo muy bien. Y al final quizás, sobre todo el primer tiempo, estuvimos con poca creación, con poca movilidad para poder hacerle más daño a Valencia. Ellos también tuvieron solamente una llegada, así que como digo, fue un partido parejo donde un golazo lo desequilibró". Pablo García y el mercado: "No, yo creo que ya eso es un tema que está para mí cerrado. Mientras estén incorporados en el plantel, van a ser jugadores que yo los voy a usar. Pablo García, Nelson Deossa, el que esté. Por otro lado, lo de Pablo son solamente especulaciones. Yo siempre digo que cada jugador que sale debilita, por supuesto, el plantel. Nos falta todavía una semana para intentar cerrar una plantilla que nos permita estar tanto en Champions como en la Liga, intentando buscar nuevamente una clasificación europea y vamos a ver cómo se da estos días. Ojalá que hubiera la menor cantidad de salidas posible". La profundidad del banquillo: "Sí, así es. Por eso tenemos un plantel ya bastante estable, un plantel bastante parecido a lo que teníamos antes. También lo dije que falta un par de retoques. Bueno, falta la Champions League y jugar muchos partidos a mitad de semana, pero creo que el plantel va por el camino correcto porque independiente de los nombres, el funcionamiento y el compromiso de cada uno de ellos es innegable durante los 90 minutos".

articles.title: Watch Lil Wayne's Son Dwayne Kick for HSFB Team on Video, Has Offer From Deion Sanders, Colorado
articles.summary: Lil Wayne may have some family company in the fame department if his son continues to kick field goals like he did in Gainesville High School's contest against Buford.
articles.body:
Lil Wayne may have some family company in the fame department if his son continues to kick field goals like he did in Gainesville High School's contest against Buford.

Dwayne Carter III, who is the son of the famous rapper, kicks for Gainesville in Georgia and buried two first-half field goals against Buford in the eventual 39-19 loss.

Hunter Shelton of On 3 noted the kicks were from 35 yards out in the first quarter and 26 yards out in the second quarter.

According to Shelton, Carter's first Division I football scholarship came from Colorado and head coach Deion Sanders. That would give him an opportunity to kick under quite a national spotlight, as the Buffaloes compete in the Big 12.

Colorado enjoyed plenty of success in the kicking department last season, as Alejandro Mata drilled 30 of his 31 extra points and 81.8 percent of his field-goal attempts. However, his eligibility expired, which was quite the loss considering his 204 career points are ninth in school history.

Perhaps Carter can be his long-term replacement if he accepts the scholarship offer.

articles.title: Pablo Maffeo al valencianismo: “Si abrimos una brecha entre afición y equipo, es lo peor que nos puede pasar; lo viví en Mallorca”
articles.standfirst: El lateral derecho debutó como titular en Mestalla y lamentó la derrota ante el Betis que no considera justa
articles.summary: El lateral derecho debutó como titular en Mestalla y lamentó la derrota ante el Betis que no considera justa
articles.body: Pablo Maffeo vivió un estreno amargo con la camiseta del Valencia. El lateral valencianista mostró su decepción tras la derrota por 0-1 frente al Betis en Mestalla, un encuentro que se resolvió en los minutos finales con el gol de Pablo García y que dejó un ambiente de tensión entre la grada, el equipo y la directiva. En declaraciones a DAZN el defensor consideró que el resultado no reflejó lo visto sobre el terreno de juego y aseguró que el conjunto de Carlos Corberán mereció un mejor desenlace. "Debut agrio. Tampoco tienes la sensación de que te hayan pegado un baile ni nada de eso. Jodido", resumió el futbolista al analizar sus primeras sensaciones tras estrenarse como valencianista. Maffeo fue uno de los jugadores más activos del equipo por el costado derecho durante gran parte del encuentro. Sin embargo, prefirió centrar el foco en el resultado colectivo antes que en su actuación individual. "Me he encontrado bien pero no es momento de pensar en mí. Prefería no haber jugado y haber sumado los tres puntos", afirmó. El lateral también expresó su desacuerdo con el resultado del partido. A su juicio, el Valencia generó suficientes oportunidades para evitar la derrota e incluso para llevarse la victoria antes de que el Betis aprovechara sus ocasiones. "No la considero justa la victoria del Betis. Hay que exigirse mucho más. Hemos tenido ocasiones para ganar o para empatar cuando estaban por delante. El fútbol es esto, contundencia en las áreas y ellos lo han sabido aprovechar", explicó. Las palabras de Maffeo llegaron después de un encuentro en el que el Valencia dispuso de varias llegadas peligrosas y rozó el empate en los instantes finales, especialmente en una clara oportunidad de Umar Sadiq que desbarató Álvaro Valles. La falta de acierto local contrastó con la eficacia del Betis, que encontró el gol de la victoria en una rápida transición culminada por Pablo García. Más allá del análisis deportivo, el defensa quiso dirigirse a la afición de Mestalla, que volvió a mostrar su malestar tras el segundo tropiezo consecutivo del equipo en apenas tres días. Maffeo reconoció el descontento de los seguidores, pero reclamó apoyo para evitar una fractura entre grada y plantilla. "Nos han animado, han estado ahí. Ellos lo ven de otra manera. Eso es así, aquí y en todos los estadios. Que nos sigan pidiendo, pero tenemos que estar todos a una", señaló. El jugador recordó experiencias vividas anteriormente en Mallorca para advertir de los riesgos que puede generar un distanciamiento entre el equipo y su entorno. "Les entiendo, pero si abrimos una brecha entre afición y equipo... me pasó en Mallorca y es lo peor que nos puede pasar. Llevo poco aquí pero les pido por favor que estén con nosotros, lo vamos a dar todo y nos vamos a enchufar. Los necesitamos de verdad", concluyó.

images.caption: Maffeo, en DAZN.

articles.title: Pablo García: "Solo pienso en el presente, en disfrutar de este día y de esta victoria"
articles.standfirst: El canterano le da los tres puntos a los de Pellegrini en Mestalla y aparca su futuro
articles.summary: El canterano le da los tres puntos a los de Pellegrini en Mestalla y aparca su futuro
articles.body: Su futuro ha estado negociándose las últimas semanas, con una oferta para salir al Hull City en la que el Betis pidió más dinero poniendo de nuevo la pelota en el tejado de los ingleses. Pero su actuación de esta noche puede cambiar por completo la situación para Pablo García. El canterano bético saltó al césped de Mestalla en los últimos minutos del partido frente al Valencia, sustituyendo a Fornals, y su impacto fue definitivo. Un golazo con la zurda para darle al Betis los tres puntos. Tras el encuentro, el atacante sevillano habló en DAZN. Valoración del partido: "Siempre los partidos aquí en Mestalla son muy difíciles. Sabíamos que el equipo venía con muchas ganas y con mucha ilusión, pero como ya comentaba, no te lo van a poner fácil ante un gran rival. Pero por suerte en esos últimos minutos finales ha podido decantarse a nuestro lado". Cómo está Pablo García: "A Pablo García yo creo que se le nota en la cara. Está feliz, está eufórico, ya no solo por el gol, que también es muy importante, ya que es el primero con el Real Betis en LaLiga, sino por la victoria del equipo, seis de seis, y no se puede pedir más". Rumores de su salida: "Yo de momento solo pienso en el presente, en disfrutar de este día y de esta victoria con el Real Betis, que es el club en el que llevo ya 15 años de mi vida. Estoy eufórico y solo pienso en la victoria y los tres puntos". El Betis se mete arriba con su pleno: "Claro. Es lo que dice el míster siempre. Todas las temporadas tenemos que dejar el club lo más alto posible, ya sea en Europa, si es en Champions o si es competir por ese título de Liga, ya que ahora, como bien has comentado, estamos segundos, pero con muchas ganas, con mucha ilusión de esta temporada y a seguir así".

articles.title: Southampton 1-4 West Ham: Josh Ajala scores debut double as Hammers hit back to reach Carabao Cup third round
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup second round tie between Southampton and West Ham United at St Mary's; two goals from Josh Ajala and one each from Taty Castellanos and Jarrod Bowen seal a comeback win on the south coast
articles.body:
Nuno Espirito Santo made it clear a cup run was not his priority by fielding a team made up of four teenagers and three 20-year-olds among eight changes from Saturday's home defeat by Charlton.

Southampton took just 10 minutes to open the scoring. Tom Fellows' looping right-wing cross was cleared only to Leo Scienza on the edge of the penalty and he showed great composure to keep the ball under pressure before calmly slotting into the far bottom corner.

Latest news and rumours: West Ham | Watch FREE PL highlights

Saints goalkeeper Daniel Peretz then made an excellent one-handed save to keep out Joel Piroe's close-range effort in the 21st minute.

West Ham equalised against the run of play four minutes before half-time when Peretz flapped at Lewis Orford's corner and 19-year-old Ayala headed home.

The Hammers took the lead eight minutes into the second half when Ayala cashed in on Jack Stephens' poor defending to fire past Peretz from eight yards.

Taty Castellanos swept in Joel Veltman's low cross 15 minutes from time before Jarrod Bowen grabbed an 84th minute fourth to condemn Southampton to a first home defeat since January 17.

"It was a very good first half and a very poor second from us.

"We had chances to go 2-0 up, conceded from a corner and from there we never found a way back into the game.

"There were some positives but as a team we need to grow and become better in a lot of different aspects."

"I am very proud of my young players and the character and belief they showed.

"It is important for Josh. He works hard every day in training to get chances in games. We are delighted he took the opportunity.

"We did not start very well but with these young lads we have to give them time and understand the process of their development.

"Winning breeds confidence and it is important now we build momentum from this and keep going."

articles.title: Plymouth Argyle 2-4 Coventry City: Frank Lampard's men survive scare to progress to Carabao Cup third round
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup second round tie between Plymouth Argyle and Coventry City at Home Park; Frank Lampard's side threw away an early two-goal lead before earning a 4-2 victory
articles.body:
City had showed their class by racing into a 2-0 lead within five minutes courtesy of goals from Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni but Argyle fought back to level nine minutes into the second half thanks to debutant Danny Irow and Xavier Amaechi.

Second-half substitute Ephron Mason-Clark scored City's third goal within five minutes of his 62nd-minute introduction before Victor Torp wrapped things up with a 78th-minute penalty.

Awoniyi fired City ahead on three minutes, picking his spot after a brilliant flick-on by Caleb Yirenkyi.

Latest news and rumours: Coventry | Watch FREE PL highlights

Yirenkyi's sublime pass on the spin from skipper Liam Kitching's through ball set striker Awoniyi on his way to goal and he had time to pick his spot to beat home goalkeeper James Storer with a side foot finish.

Within two minutes City increased their lead following a lightning break down the right. Awoniyi set Rudoni racing on his way to goal and he made no mistake, again beating Storer with a clinical finish, this time from the edge of the box.

Jake Bidwell came close to making it 3-0 on the 18th minute, heading just past the post from Joel Latibeaudiere's pinpoint cross to the far post.

Argyle responded in the 21st minute through Irow, who cut in from the left and beat Latibeaudiere, before sending a low shot past City keeper Daniel Bentley into the far corner.

Midfielder Harvey White had sent Irow - who has just joined Plymouth on loan from Tottenham - away down the left with a superb pass from his own half after spotting the winger out wide.

The unmarked Awoniyi could have doubled his tally on 27 minutes but headed wide from six yards from Latibeaudiere's deep cross.

Striker Will Evans' effort flew off the foot of Bentley and on to a post in the 31st minute after the keeper had failed to hold White's long-range effort.

Argyle restored parity on 54 minutes when half-time sub Amaechi won the ball from City defender Kitching and raced into the box before beating Bentley with a thumping low drive into the corner.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto volleyed just over from Mason-Clark's cross in the 65th minute before the latter restored City's lead in the 67th minute from close range, turning in Torp's thumping cross.

Torp gave Coventry some breathing space by converting a penalty following a foul by sub Joe Edwards on Brandon Thomas-Asante, who could have increased City's lead in stoppage time but hammered his volley over from the edge of the six-yard box.

"It was an entertaining cup tie. It was never in our plan to conceded two goals in the first four minutes.

"We showed a lot of resilience in pre-season, defensive records are what you can build results on so we need to be strong defensively.

"The reaction to that, losing two goals so early, was excellent. I couldn't be happier with the players.

"I thought all four debutants were good. Oli Irow gives us something different. He wants to take players on, good pace and he's direct.

"I thought Tyreeq Bakinson look assured and Joe Mwaro was excellent on his debut. It's a night he will never forget against top opposition and James Storer in goal.

"Then you bring on Xavier Amaechi and he looked sharp, motivated. There were a lot of good performances out there.

"This is what you want from cup ties, I have got a healthy headache ahead of Saturday's league game against Bradford.

"We have lost a game which I never want to do but we are in a healthier place. I thought as a team we showed more personality. We took the hand brake off."

"You have always got to enjoy a win but at this point it is also looking at performance and individual and collective performances.

"We made a lot of changes and so for me it's good to have a look at players that we didn't start at the weekend (Friday) and are pushing for places.

"I expected it to be difficult, it's not an easy place to come. It was a great start to the game, two really good goals, high quality goals.

"Exactly what we want running through back lines and just showing good capacity to run and good combination stuff as well.

"Maybe we relaxed or something but we didn't put our foot down. When you get teams in that situation you should go and put your foot properly down and we didn't.

"In an early round in the cup it can happen. Big mistakes for the goals, we must be honest about that, and then a good reaction to win the game pretty well.

"Ephron is a big player for us so it was good to see him looking strong. He wants to get better all the time.

"But of course a win is a big deal because it's a nice feeling to take back on the bus for four hours."

articles.title: Stoke City 1-1 Hull City (4-5 pens): Tigers follow up Man Utd win with shootout victory in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup second round tie between Stoke City and Hull City at the bet365 Stadium; George Hirst missed the only penalty in the shootout to see Hull progress after the game finished 1-1 after 90 minutes
articles.body:
Robert Bozenik opened the scoring for the hosts before the Tigers equalised through Kieran Dowell on the stroke of half time.

With neither side able to force a winner, Hull ran out 5-4 winners on penalties.

Sergej Jakirovic made 11 changes to the side that stunned Manchester United at the weekend, handing full debuts to Lucas Herrington and Matt Targett, as well as midfield pair Jens Hjerto-Dahl and Lucas Gourna-Douath.

Latest news and rumours: Hull | Watch FREE PL highlights

It was a bright start from Hull, and Hjerto-Dahl in particular, who opened his body up and curled an effort towards the far post which was pushed wide by Josh Griffiths.

Paddy McNair then headed Liam Millar's corner wide at the back post as the visitors enjoyed the best of the opening exchanges.

After losing their opening two Championship games of the season, including a 2-1 defeat to Swansea at the bet365 Stadium on the opening day, Mark Robins made seven changes as Bozenik, Luke Graham, Ben Pearson, Tomas Rigo, Million Manhoef and Laurence Giani were all handed starts.

Stoke had reportedly turned down a bid from the Tigers for star winger Sorba Thomas, and it was the Wales international who created the opener when he cut in from the left and whipped a cross in that was met by Bozenik.

The Slovakian scored the only goal when the pair last met on New Year's Day, and the forward brushed aside McNair to head Stoke in front.

Griffiths had been given the nod in goal as Viktor Johansson was given the night off and the former West Brom stopper beat away Dowell's first effort from distance as half-time loomed.

But the former Rangers man wasn't to be denied a second time as he lashed home after he was picked out by Millar.

David Akintola was making his first appearance for Hull since January and spurred two golden chances to put them ahead after the break.

The Nigerian firstly steered Targett's cross wide of the right-hand post before rounding Griffiths and firing into the side-netting after he was played in by Millar.

The forward then saw his next sight of goal comfortably saved by Griffiths.

With nothing to separate the sides at the end of 90 minutes, it was to be a penalty shootout that decided the tie.

New Stoke signing George Hirst saw his tame penalty kept out by Dillon Phillips, while Hull converted all five of their spot kicks as Mohamed Belloumi sent the Tigers into round three for the first time in six years.

"I thought we played alright. There were hardly any clear-cut openings in the game other than one or two mistakes, they'd had a bit of a sight of the goal, we'd had a bit of a sight of the goal.

"Our goal was really good. The movement was brilliant in the box and the cross was really good, the cross finds him and he [Bozenik] scores again against Hull.

"I want to see us grow in real confidence and then try and boss games, and I thought we bossed the game. We were pretty good.

"We gave a goal away that was just typical of us really. It was a poor goal. We don't win the first one, don't win the second one, gets played wide, ball gets played in, we're too deep and we miss tackles.

"I thought we were the better of the two teams, I thought we were good. There's some young players in there making their debuts.

"To lose on penalties is no disgrace, the penalties were generally pretty good apart from the one you miss, which is never great.

"We've got to take out what we can, which is some decent performances, some good minutes into legs and the fact we've come through unscathed."

"We broke one more record, so now I have two penalty shootouts in a row!

"It was an opportunity for other players to play, and after Manchester United there was a lot of excitement, a lot of stress, a few problems with some players so I will use this competition to give other players a chance because you never know when we will need them.

"We used this game for [Hidemasa] Morita, for [Lucas] Gourna-Douath, for Jens [Hjerto-Dahl], also Abdulkadir [Omur], [David] Akintola, also Cody [Drameh]. For young [Lucas] Herrington it was great for adaptation to English football - intensity, dynamic, everything we need for the future.

"Akintola could have had a hat-trick but he showed a lot of effort, energy, he tried to press with Dowell and just missed at least one goal."

articles.title: Ipswich Town 3-1 Leicester City: Marcelino Nunez's stunning strike from centre-circle send Tractor Boys through in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup second round tie between Ipswich Town and Leicester City at Portman Road; Marcelino Nunez scored a contender for goal of the season as Gary O'Neil's side run out 3-1 winners
articles.body:
This had been a Premier League fixture only 15 months ago, but Leicester arrived at Portman Road fresh from a painful home loss to Burton in League One and yet under-fire Russell Martin watched the Foxes edge a goalless first half.

Sindre Walle Egeli showed Premier League quality for Gary O'Neil's team with a smart left-footed finish to break the deadlock after 62 minutes before 19-year-old Olabade Aluko earned Leicester a deserved leveller five minutes later.

Latest news and rumours: Ipswich | Watch FREE PL highlights

However, ex-Norwich midfielder Nunez fittingly had the final say in the meeting between two former Canaries team-mates.

Nunez rifled home off a post after 71 minutes to score for the first time at Portman Road since his move last summer and added a wonderful 50-yard lob in stoppage time to help Ipswich reach the Carabao Cup third round for only the second time in 11 seasons.

Martin was booed after Leicester lost to Burton and watched his team almost gift an opener inside 33 seconds, but Chuba Akpom could not profit.

Leicester, to their credit, quickly settled and Brighton loanee Tom Watson sent one shot wide before he tested Christian Walton with a curled effort.

Ipswich back-up goalkeeper Walton thwarted Christian McFarlane's attempted chip in the 20th minute after a lovely Louis Page pass and at the other end Jakub Stolarczyk made a fine save from Dara O'Shea's header.

However, Leicester finished the half strongly when Conor Chaplin's curler was pushed wide by Walton.

Ipswich midfielder Kasey McAteer had a goal ruled out for offside two minutes after half-time before Chaplin was withdrawn to a standing ovation on the hour mark by Martin, who then watched the home side break the deadlock in the 62nd minute.

Akpom played through to Jack Clarke and he squared for Egeli to slot home.

Five minutes later, Leicester equalised when Page's corner was flicked on by Bobby De Cordova-Reid and 19-year-old Aluko got a faint touch to score his first professional goal.

Nunez ensured there would be no upset when he fired in via a post after Woyo Coulibaly had given the ball away and after Akpom squandered a one-on-one chance, the Chile international grabbed a second.

After the ball dropped inside the centre circle, Nunez spotted Stolarczyk off his line and lobbed over the Leicester goalkeeper in incredible fashion to make it back-to-back wins for O'Neil.

"I didn't think it was the best decision to be honest!

"Neither did Chuba (Akpom) or Sindre who were clean through on goal, but as long as you can put it in the goal no one can argue, so good decision in the end!

"The last two performances Marcelino has been excellent. Two great goals, unbelievable energy that he has, never stops and unbelievably humble kid that works and works.

"You need them in your group and two big moments of quality to add to that which changed the game for us.

"He is in a good spot and need to keep him going. We need to keep him going for the weekend and it is now a big push to get everyone going on Sunday (at Manchester United)."

"The players were amazing and I loved it. I loved the performance.

"We were unlucky to lose and definitely unlucky to lose 3-1, but after Saturday we spoke a lot about bravery, aggression and intensity. With and without the ball they showed so much.

"The only thing missing is we didn't win but if we play like that, it is really exciting for us. We'll have a lot of fun and win a lot of games.

"It is so early and that is why I feel really calm about it. The fans were amazing as well. Hopefully they felt a bit of energy after that performance."

articles.title: Akron announces its 'Offensive Coordinator of the Game,' who will help Joe Moorhead script opening drive vs. Robert Morris
articles.summary: Martin Alan Whims II, a former Akron student and longtime Zips season-ticket holder, won the viral contest the program launched this month.
articles.body:
Week 2 of this year's college football slate features games between Ohio State and Texas, Oklahoma and Michigan, BYU and Arizona, Texas A&M and Arizona State, Kentucky and Alabama, as well as Tennessee and Georgia Tech.

An afternoon matchup pitting FCS Robert Morris against Akron is also circled on the calendar.

The first drive, at least, will be appointment television — on ESPN+, that is. Akron is entrusting Martin Alan Whims II to be the "Offensive Coordinator of the Game." Whims, an Akron grad and longtime Zips season-ticket holder, will help head coach Joe Moorhead script the Zips' opening series of their home opener on Sept. 12.

Whims won a viral contest among Akron football season-ticket holders that debuted this summer. A random drawing, in which participating candidates earned an extra chance to win with every new season-ticket holder they referred, whittled the pool down to nine contenders last week. Among that lucky group was Barstool Sports personality Dan "Big Cat" Katz, the host of the podcast "Pardon My Take," and popular YouTuber James Bordeaux, who has grown a significant following rebuilding teams on college football video game titles, including EA Sports College Football 27.

The Zips announced Whims as the winner on Tuesday.

🚨IT'S OFFICIAL... Martin Allan Whims II is named OC of the Game presented by @Arbys Steak Nuggets‼️ #GoZips 🦘 #MakeTheClimb pic.twitter.com/3VHtodEq07 — Akron Football (@ZipsFB) August 25, 2026

🚨IT'S OFFICIAL... Martin Allan Whims II is named OC of the Game presented by @Arbys Steak Nuggets‼️ #GoZips 🦘 #MakeTheClimb pic.twitter.com/3VHtodEq07

When Akron football first posted to X about the contest on Aug. 4, news of the opportunity spread like wildfire. That inaugural post now has 23.1 million views. It wasn't long before the Zips saw a significant uptick in season-ticket sales , and, according to a program release , they've sold out InfoCision Stadium's suites for the first time.

The Akron Beacon Journal's Nate Ulrich explored the origin of the contest and what exactly it will look like in a comprehensive piece for the outlet .

The school's athletic director, Andrew T. Goodrich, told the Beacon Journal that the idea of the promotion stemmed from a brainstorming session on a trip back from the NCAA men's basketball tournament. He wanted to cultivate the same kind of energy Zips fans showed during March Madness when the football season rolled around.

"It just maybe was such a late night and long day, and maybe we were delirious, but we just believed it could work and thought this is really cool," said Matt Pottorff, Akron senior deputy AD and chief operating officer, per the Beacon Journal.

"We knew that we needed to wait until the right time, though, and so we've had this idea [for months] before we launched it. We just wanted to make sure it was going to be the right time before the season started. We thought we were going to have maybe a lull in the media, and we could at best maybe get a million views."

Goodrich and Pottorff's lightbulb moment created a much greater impression than that, but it wasn't ever going to work without the approval of Moorhead, an accomplished coach who has previously coordinated offenses at the likes of Oregon and Penn State.

At first, Moorhead, now in his fifth season as the Zips' head coach, was staunchly against the concept; however, he quickly warmed up to it once he understood the guardrails that would be put in place. It's important to keep in mind that Moorhead doesn't have an OC on staff at the moment and that he is the team's play-caller.

That isn't changing, not even for the jointly scripted drive in Week 2, except Moorhead told the Beacon Journal that he doesn't want to "shortchange" the contest winner.

"I'm going to sit this person down, and I'm going to actually take them through the Robert Morris scouting report," Moorhead said. "I'm going to show them their tendencies on first and second down by formation. [I'll say], 'These are the plays that we like for each formation. This is how I've constructed the openers to attack them and why. Let's see what you have and if there's anything that we're able to kind of translate into our system or terminology.'"

He continued, per the Beacon Journal : "I'm going to have the openers scripted, and they're going to have their ideas. I don't know if it would be a reordering, or, quite frankly, they may have a freaking great idea that fits what we do offensively. And I'll say, 'Alright, well, let's substitute that play for this one.'"

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

NFL Players returning to college + QB Battles settled + Big 10 takes a stand

Moorhead, naturally, will have the final say. That doesn't mean Whims won't have his own stamp on a much-discussed opening drive less than three weeks from now.

"It's super cool," Whims said in a video Akron posted to X on Tuesday before expounding on how even being considered a finalist has created a good bit of buzz in his life. "My boss shared it on LinkedIn, so I was getting business contacts reaching out, friends, family — everybody's just super excited about it."

He added: "Even if I hadn't had got it, it would have been an awesome experience. Winning the whole thing is just awesome. Super excited for it."

articles.title: LASK 5-1 Celtic (agg 5-4): Hoops throw away four-goal aggregate lead as stunning collapse ends Champions League group stage hopes
articles.summary: Report as Celtic are dumped out of the Champions League after throwing away a four-goal aggregate lead to LASK; Celtic took the lead on the night through Callum McGregor but LASK scored five to deny them a spot in Thursday's draw; Celtic to play Europa League football again
articles.body:
In one of the worst nights in Celtic's European history, the Hoops were up 4-0 on aggregate after Callum McGregor extended their 3-0 first-leg advantage early on in Austria.

Despite wobbling after goals from Moses Usor, Robert Ljubicic and a Samuel Adeniran stunner, Celtic were minutes from booking a place in Thursday's League phase draw before second-half substitute Florian Flecker headed home a 90th-minute equaliser to force extra-time.

Full of all the energy and desire that Celtic whimpered at the sight of, the momentum belonged to the Austrian champions. Adeniran struck from range again in the 109th minute to put LASK in front on aggregate for the first time.

He very nearly added salt to Celtic's wounds when he stepped up for a penalty moments later, after Reo Hatate fouled Krystof Danek deep, but Viljami Sinisalo kept the spot-kick out to give his side a lifeline.

It was a lifeline that went begging as the full-time whistle confirmed Celtic would miss out on the Champions League for the second consecutive season. Last season it was defeat on penalties at this stage to Kairat Almaty.

This year's failure, given the context of a four-goal aggregate lead, will take considerably longer to move on from.

Once again the Hoops will be involved in the Europa League league-phase draw on Friday.

6: BIG CHANCE! Celtic move it quickly up the field. Yang plays a ball into the area that Baur latches onto, poking wide of the mark with Hogh running in.

20: LASK CHANCES! The first falls to Mbuyamba in the area, who can't quite match the flight of the ball to send it goalwards. Any touch on that and Lask would have had a goal. The second has Sinisalo worried, as it strikes the post.

21: GOAL! It's a smart, smart low strike from McGregor but it takes a nick off Andrade and flies past Jungwirth in the LASK goal.

32: GOAL! IT'S A GIFT! Celtic punished for complacent play at the back. Nygren passes a ball back into no man's land, putting it on a plate for Usor to stroke past Sinisalo.

48: GOAL! LASK LEAD! Lask are beginning to believe. Ljubicic beats Sinisalo from range with a superb low strike from the edge of the area.

58: GOAL! WHAT A FINISH!!! That is simply superb technique. No chance Sinisalo was getting anywhere near that. The LASK striker is teed up outside the box and curls home.

90: GOAL! LASK MAKE IT FOUR TO SEND IT TO EXTRA TIME! Sinisalo does brilliantly to deny Joao Victor Tornich initially, but he can do nothing about the rebound as Florian Flecker heads home to make it 4-4 on aggregate!

108: GOAL! Nightmare stuff for Celtic as Adeniran strikes from range again. LASK now lead on aggregate.

114: FROM BAD TO WORSE! Hatate brings down Danek in the box gives away a penalty!

Celtic boss Martin O'Neill speaking with Amazon Prime :

"We should've been out of sight by half-time. We missed two great opportunities and then we gave them a lifeline right before half-time and then another one just after it. They came roaring back. That's my team, that's my responsibility.

"At half-time I thought we were still well in command of the game. Just after they score and then momentum goes in their direction. It's hard to stem it when they're chasing the game and we can't get out for 10 minutes.

"These are tough games. This might have been a qualification game but it felt like a Champions League game. That doesn't matter. Talking about the squad is for another day.

"It's a massive disappointment. We're playing in the Europa League but that's no consolation this evening. There was a feel good factor and that's a massive disappointment tonight."

Celtic 's Callum McGregor speaking with Amazon Prime:

"We got what we deserved. I thought we were passive all night. We actually looked scared to go and win the game.

"To be honest, I don't think we were that good in the first leg either and we kind of got away with it. But then you're up 3-0 and think you have a chance. When you play like that, you can't have any excuse whatsoever.

"We have to suck it up. We apologise to the supporters and to the club because there's no way we should lose that game. Now we have to see what character we have.

"You can't lose the game by such a big margin and look for excuses elsewhere. This is where we see what people are made of in terms of what we achieve this season."

Your views: 'Celtic were hapless, hopeless and humiliated'

LJJ: " Absolutely embarrassing for Celtic, maybe Europa League is the level for them since they get into the CL with ease every year but don't make an impact when actually in it. Maybe that's their level, but I don't think they deserve Europe at all after what I've just witnessed!"

Jonny: " Celtic got what they deserved. They didn't exactly play well last week and were lucky to come away with three goals and decided to park the bus, just not good enough."

Reinaldo7: " Don't know whether to laugh or cry. Worse than last year against Kairat. Strange choices for subs tonight. Hang your heads in shame boys, they weren't that special but made us look ordinary. More work needed if we are to succeed in Europe."

Stevo: " I think this was worse than Kairat. Yes, it's not ideal losing on penalties to them, but to be 4-0 up and throw that all away, that's impressively shocking!"

jcluk: " No more LASK chances for Celtic. They were hapless, hopeless and humiliated. Can see them struggling domestically too this season."

articles.title: Nottingham Forest 0-2 Leeds United: Visitors earn second win at City Ground in three days in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Leeds United won at Nottingham Forest for second time in three days to book their spot in the Carabao Cup third round; second-half goals from Dan James and James Justin sealed the win
articles.body:
Daniel Farke's side took the three Premier League points home on Saturday and earned a 2-0 victory in the League Cup thanks to goals from Dan James and James Justin.

Having not won at the City Ground since 1972 before the weekend, they have now triumphed there twice in 72 hours as the Yorkshire club enjoy a winning start to the new campaign.

Latest news and rumours: Leeds | Forest | Watch FREE PL highlights

It is not the start new Forest boss Oliver Glasner was looking for as things are yet to click, though additions are on the way with a £50m deal agreed for Chelsea striker Liam Delap .

Neither side will have been jumping for joy at the prospect of a rematch so soon after Saturday's Premier League opener.

But Forest enjoyed some early promise as James Trafford was forced into a great save in the 10th minute when he had to fend away Ola Aina's cross-shot, which almost left him wrongfooted.

Then Justin was in the right place at the right time to stop Igor Jesus' header from going in.

Leeds came into it and should have gone in front midway through the first half when James got in down the right, but his pull-back was just behind Sean Longstaff, who shot straight at Matz Sels.

Both sides were going for it and Leeds defender Joe Rodon denied Chris Wood with a brilliant last-ditch tackle while Sels kept out James' low effort at the other end.

The Wales international showed the required composure five minutes after the restart.

Aina's wayward header allowed Longstaff to gallop forward and he played in James, who clipped home.

Forest almost hit straight back as Arnaud Kalimuendo's cutback was perfect for Wood, but Trafford did brilliantly to stop his effort from going into the bottom corner, before Noah Okafor sent an effort just wide as Leeds staged a rapid counter-attack.

Leeds sealed the victory with 15 minutes remaining but there was nothing pretty about it.

Lucas Nmecha tried to claim it as his bundled effort was blocked on the line by Williams, with Justin finally putting the ball into the back of the net.

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner told Sky Sports

"This is a little bit the assessment after six weeks here, that maybe - and not just in the team, it's maybe in the club - that there's a little bit of ignoring the reality.

"Right now, we are far away from where we want to be, and what I'm really convinced in that where we will be.

"The fact is that this team had a relegation battle for nine months. Very turbulent season and it ended with a huge effort to stay in the league, and this is our starting point.

"It's really very important not to blame anybody because sometimes I tell them facts and they say, 'Oh, Glasner is complaining'.

"No, no, no. But then maybe your best midfielder [Elliot Anderson] leaves the club and now we expect we compete for European places because Oliver Glasner is in. Sorry, this is what I can't deliver within six weeks.

"I'm no magician, no messiah, just hard work. That is what we have to do.

"It doesn't make sense talking about seventh two years ago. It's hard, it's tough, but if you ignore the reality then you live in dreamland and this is never the best thing to do."

Leeds boss Daniel Farke told Sky Sports:

"This is what we came for, and this was my main goal.

"You play a cup run to go through. Very happy with the level of the performance, because we had to wait very long for a win here at Nottingham and to do this two times within three days at such a tough ground, this remarkable level of performance was outstanding.

"Saturday was really a tight game, but today I think it's not in doubt that it was a fully deserved win."

articles.title: Birmingham City 1-6 Brentford: Callum Wilson scores six minutes into full debut as Keith Andrews' Bees run riot at St Andrew's
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup second round tie between Birmingham City and Brentford at St Andrew's; the Bees saunter into round three thanks to two goals from Nathan Collins and one each from Callum Wilson, Aaron Hickey, Mikkel Damsgaard and Igor Thiago
articles.body:
The 34-year-old Wilson, who joined on a free transfer from relegated West Ham, seized his first opportunity with a crisp finish which took a deflection off defender Dael Fry, who had a debut to forget.

Brentford's Premier League quality was evident throughout and although Blues equalised through Demarai Gray just before the half-hour they were level for just seven minutes.

Latest news and rumours: Brentford | Watch FREE PL highlights

Lax defending saw Aaron Hickey and Collins score in quick succession to effectively seal the tie before half-time, with Mikkel Damsgaard getting on the end of a counter-attack to add the fourth.

Igor Thiago's smart close-range finish sent fans streaming for the exit, missing Collins' second header.

The Bees, quarter-finalists last season, had not beaten Birmingham in six previous meetings, the last a goalless draw more than five years ago in the Championship before they went on to bigger and better things which their ambitious hosts now hope to emulate.

Birmingham's priority remains promotion so, after opening with two league draws, boss Chris Davies made six changes, including goalkeeper Ryan Allsop, Fry and Argentinian striker Luis Vazquez.

However, the gulf to a Premier League squad was evident as Keith Andrews retained only three of the team which demolished Tottenham and saw three of his newcomers score and another, Yehor Yarmoliuk, run the midfield before he was forced off with injury.

Davies wants to meet the club's aspirations by playing their way out of the Championship but it proved their undoing before they had even had chance to get a foothold in the game as they fell foul of Brentford's high press at a short goal-kick.

Paik Seung-ho was slow to react to the loose ball and Yarmoliuk played in Wilson to fire home first-time from the edge of the area with the aid of a deflection.

But a miscontrol by Jannik Schuster saw the centre-back booked for bringing down Vazquez and from Paik's short free-kick Gray drilled a deflected shot through a crowd of players.

It was a brief moment of joy in an otherwise chastening night as a failure to deal with Vitaly Janelt's chip and Wilson's strength allowed Hickey to fire home an angled shot.

Collins jumped in front of Fry to nod in a simple header from Jaidon Anthony's cross but a ruthless Brentford went for the kill and, after bringing on the likes of Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Mamadou Sangare, scored three more after the break.

"My message to supporters tonight is 'sorry'. It's not very pleasant and I can understand how frustrating it is for them.

"It was a very tough evening for us, a painful evening, and incredibly disappointing to lose a game 6-1 at home.

"There were many situations where we were just not good enough to compete and I take ultimate responsibility for it - and the players will have to do it in their own minds.

"We were beaten by a team a long way ahead of us in every aspect. Was 6-1 a fair reflection? Probably."

"I didn't really blink an eyelid making so many changes.

"There is a huge narrative around cup games with coaches making changes but with the squad we have, there are fine margins between who plays and doesn't play.

"We needed to compete really hard to play the game we wanted. I thought overall we produced a really good performance."

articles.title: Julián, un tormento de 90 días
articles.standfirst: La situación del argentino explotó a finales de mayo… más de tres meses después no hay solución que satisfaga a todas las partes
articles.summary: La situación del argentino explotó a finales de mayo… más de tres meses después no hay solución que satisfaga a todas las partes
articles.body: El 25 de mayo los cimientos del Atlético temblaron cuando MARCA desveló lo que, desde ese momento, quedó en evidencia de que iba a ser el culebrón del verano: Julián había pedido salir del club de manera oficial con un único destino: seguir su carrera en LaLiga defendiendo los colores del Barcelona. Casi 100 días después, la situación permanece igual de encallada. Quizá todavía peor después de ver la esperada reacción del Metropolitano a todo lo acontecido durante estos tres meses eternos. Un verdadero tormento para todas las partes que alcanzó su punto álgido en ruido ante el Villarreal, en el reencuentro del todavía rojiblanco con una afición que le tenía como su estandarte hasta que explotó la decisión de Julián de no querer seguir luciendo la rojiblanca. Mas de tres meses de auténtica locura en los que habló La Araña el 22 de junio pese a estar en la disputa de un Mundial, en los que los rojiblancos afearon públicamente las maniobras del Barça y en los que hasta Miguel Ángel Gil tuvo que tomar la palabra en tres ocasiones para hacer oficial el sentir en los despachos del Metropolitano: Julián no sale del club. Cierto es que desde que estalló la bomba lo que se ha deslizado desde los despachos del Metropolitano no ha variado un ápice: “Contamos con Julián, no va a salir”, decían los que más conocen un caso al que le queda el hilo de vida que dan los últimos días del mercado de fichajes. La solución, en todo caso, se antoja imposible. Los rojiblancos no abren en ningún momento la puerta que quiere el delantero: la del Barça. Un sueño por cumplir que tiene cero visos de acabar siendo realidad pese a que el futbolista desliza todavía a su entorno más cercano que es donde quiere jugar esta campaña 26-27. El laberinto, así las cosas, queda con el Arsenal como única salida. Pero es el propio futbolista el que no quiere regresar a una Premier en la que ya defendió la elástica del Manchester City… pero donde no quiere acabar donde quizá sería la única salida a este tormento que ya supera los 90 días.

articles.title: Rafael Márquez ya tiene a sus jugadores para ‘renovar’ a la Selección Mexicana: Chivas y América las apuestas
articles.standfirst: Se viene el debut como entrenador del que fuera el capitán histórico del Tri
articles.summary: Se viene el debut como entrenador del que fuera el capitán histórico del Tri
articles.body: Falta un mes para que Rafael Márquez debute como entrenador de la Selección Mexicana, luego de auxiliar a Javier Aguirre rumbo y durante el Mundial 2026. El rival para esa presentación será Colombia, que en el último entre ellos goleó al conjunto mexicano 4-0 en octubre de 2025 en Arlington, Texas. Si bien faltan cuatro semanas para el primer partido de cuatro en la próxima ventana de la FIFA, Rafa Márquez tendrá que presentar su lista en un par de semanas para atender los tiempos que requieren los clubes. Y ahí se vendrán unas sorpresas en la convocatoria, adelanta David Medrano, de TV Azteca, aunque la base será la misma que estuvo en la Copa del Mundo, donde se quedó eliminado en octavos de final ante Inglaterra en el Estadio Azteca. Los nuevos nombres serían Hugo Camberos y Santiago Sandoval, ambos de Chivas y que consiguieran el boleto a Los Ángeles 2028 hace unas semanas, así como Iván Tona, mediocampista de Tijuana. También se sumaría desde el América Isaías Violante y se regresaría al Tri Alan Cervantes, también azulcrema, quien no ha sido convocado desde 2021, cuando jugó la Copa Oro. Pero Rafa Márquez tiene un problema que debe decidir antes de dar a conocer su primera lista, misma en la que estará condicionado. Ese primer partido contra Colombia se jugará el sábado 26 de septiembre en el M&T Bank Stadium de Baltimore, pero ese fin de semana la Liga MX tendrá su jornada 10, por lo que el seleccionador solo podrá llamar máximo a dos futbolista por equipo mexicano y a partir del lunes 28 ya puede llamar a otros que juegan en México. Ahí está la duda: si llamará para el primer partido ante los colombianos a los novatos para su proceso o se irá con los experimentados para afrontar su debut en el banquillo tricolor.

articles.title: Corberán: “Es injusto pedirle paciencia a la afición de Mestalla”
articles.standfirst: El técnico agradece el apoyo de la grada y reclama fichajes en ataque
articles.summary: El técnico agradece el apoyo de la grada y reclama fichajes en ataque
articles.body: Carlos Corberán estaba dolido tras la derrota ante el Betis. El técnico del Valencia defendía que la propuesta de cinco jugadores en la retaguardia era válida para evitar pérdidas en campo propio, donde más daño hace el equipo verdiblanco, y que el gol del rival llegó en una contra no en un ataque posicional. El técnico del Valencia explicó que espera que lleguen refuerzos en la zona de ataque y que el equipo pueda seguir mejorando con las últimas incorporaciones. ¿No cree que la defensa de cinco le da solidez al equipo, pero le cueta mucho más en ataque? “Lo que yo quería es evitar pérdidas no forzadas para no exigirnos en defensa. La línea de cinco no ha impedido que ganara el partido. Teníamos que evitar pérdidas no forzadas. El inicio del partido ha sido muy bueno y para generar ocasiones es importante quitarle el balón al rival. Nos han marcado en una contra”. Ambiente crispado en la grada, ¿le pide paciencia a la afición? “Es injusto perdirle paciencia a la afición. El ambiente ha sido sensacional, nos han apoyado desde el minuto uno para superar la adversidad de jugar con un día menos de descanso. Ganar partidos es lo que quieren. El ambiente de Mestalla ha sido sensacional. El equipo se ha vaciado hasta el final. No queremos nada más que ganar en Mestalla. Nos quedamos dolidos y aceptamos la crítica. Tenemos que seguir mejorando para conseguir más rédito y ganar partidos”. El público ha pedido fichajes, ¿cuántas piezas le faltan al equipo? “En la parte de arriba hay que ver las posibilidades de incorporar a uno o varios jugadores. Lo de Arnau está cerca, pero el foco está en las posiciones de ataque. El club quiere cerrar el mercado en esa parcela del equipo" ¿Qué hay que hacer para ganar? “Ganar en el fútbol es mejorar las diferentes momentos en el juego. Nos ha costado mantener la energía inicial. Tenemos que trabajar la consistencia ofensiva y defensiva del equipo. Hemos hecho méritos suficientes para no haber perdido el partido. Tras el gol el equipo no se ha venido abajo. Otorbi ha dejado buenas sensaciones”. ¿Qué le parece el ambiente de Mestalla tras el final? “Entiendo la frustración de la afición con nosotros, pero hasta la última jugada el apoyo ha sido excelente. Tenemos que vaciarnos en el campo. No siento que estemos en el derecho de pedirles nada a la afición. La afición siente esa frustración. Eso forma parte de nuestro trabajo".

Fernandes finished with 21 Premier League assists, breaking a record previously shared by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne, while also scoring nine goals as United secured third place and a return to the Champions League under manager Michael Carrick.But his dominance was not confined to the individual award.Fernandes was also selected in the PFA Premier League Team of the Year, where he was one of only two players from outside Arsenal and Manchester City to make the XI. The other was Brentford striker Igor Thiago.Fernandes completes the individual-award hat-trickFernandes' PFA triumph is the latest recognition of a season in which he consistently stood out despite United's struggles in previous campaigns.His record-breaking assist tally reached 21 on the final day of the Premier League season, when he provided the delivery for Patrick Dorgu's header against Brighton.That moved him beyond the previous joint record of 20 assists held by Henry and De Bruyne and gave Fernandes the outright Premier League record for assists in a single season.He finished the campaign with nine goals as United climbed to third in the table, securing Champions League qualification.The PFA award carries a particular significance because it is voted for by fellow professional footballers.Fernandes, who attended Tuesday night's ceremony with his wife Ana, admitted that receiving recognition from players he competes against made the achievement particularly meaningful.âIt is obviously a very proud moment,â Fernandes said. âThey are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment.âHis win also restored United's presence at the top of the PFA's individual awards after a 16-year wait. articles.title: Akron Reveals Fan to Serve as OC for 1st Drive of CFB Season Opener After Viral Contest
articles.summary: Akron has named its "Offensive Coordinator of the Game" for its home opener against Robert Morris after a viral contest decided who gets to call plays on the opening drive of the game.
articles.body:
Akron has named its "Offensive Coordinator of the Game" for its home opener against Robert Morris after a viral contest decided who gets to call plays on the opening drive of the game.

The team revealed that Martin Allan Whims II will help Zips head coach Joe Moorhead script offensive plays on the opening drive on Sept. 12.

Akron announced earlier this month that it would hold a contest that gave one lucky season-ticket holder a chance to script plays for the opening drive in the team's home opener.

The contest was clearly a tactic to drive up season-ticket sales, and it worked. In the days after the contest was revealed, the team sold out its suite inventory for the first time in program history.

Akron senior deputy athletic director and COO Matt Pottorff told Ellyn Briggs of Front Office Sports that the school had far exceeded its season-ticket sales goal just days after the contest was announced.

Pottorff also said the team wouldn't let the fan go in completely blind.

"First, we're going to call that person NFL draft–style and let them know that they got selected. Then we'll find a time for them to come to campus, where they'll meet with [head football] coach Joe Moorhead," he said. "He'll run them through what plays we would normally call in the opening drive, and then figure out what they want to do with it."

While the fan, Whims, doesn't have a background in college football coaching, he's well-versed in Akron football. Per Nate Urlich of the Akron Beacon Journal , he has held season tickets since InfoCision Stadium opened in 2009.

Whether Whims will have success dialing up plays for Akron remains to be seen, but it's safe to say Akron's season-ticket promotion achieved what it set out to accomplish.

articles.title: "Hay pocos casos como el de Chicharito": la Hormiga González recibe contundente mensaje tras llegar a Olympiacos
articles.standfirst: Armando González comenzará su aventura por Europa
articles.summary: Armando González comenzará su aventura por Europa
articles.body: La Hormiga González ya vive sus primeros días como jugador del Olympiacos de Grecia y espera hacer su debut este fin de semana, cuando su nuevo equipo visite al Asteras en la Superliga de Grecia. El delantero mexicano ya se ha dejado ver en los primeros entrenamientos con el conjunto griego, donde comienza su adaptación al futbol europeo. Cabe recordar que el pasado sábado se hizo oficial su fichaje por alrededor de 12 millones de euros, además de que Chivas mantendrá un 20% de una futura venta. De esta manera, la Hormiga da el gran salto al futbol europeo después de una temporada espectacular en la Liga MX, en la que marcó 24 goles y conquistó el título de goleo, actuaciones que también le permitieron ser considerado por la Selección Mexicana para disputar la Copa del Mundo. La llegada de la Hormiga González al futbol de Grecia ha generado opiniones divididas. Mientras algunos consideran que el delantero de Chivas pudo haber elegido un destino más competitivo, otros creen que su llegada al Olympiacos representa una gran oportunidad para comenzar su aventura por Europa. Lo que es un hecho es que el canterano rojiblanco ya dio el paso y un club europeo apostó fuerte por él. Ahora, Miguel Layún, quien tuvo una importante trayectoria en el futbol europeo, le mandó un consejo al atacante mexicano. Además, el exfutbolista de la Selección Mexicana y del Club América señaló que González tendrá que ir a Europa a competir y demostrar su nivel, pues su llegada al futbol europeo le permitirá tener mayor exposición y ser observado por clubes de otras ligas. Layún destacó que el futbol mexicano no tiene el mismo alcance en Europa, por lo que ahora la Hormiga tendrá una vitrina mucho más importante para continuar con su crecimiento. En el caso de Nery Castillo, tuvo un gran recorrido con el Olympiacos, donde permaneció siete temporadas y conquistó nueve títulos. Posteriormente, dio el salto al Shakhtar Donetsk de Ucrania y, más tarde, tuvo una etapa con el Manchester City. Un camino que, de alguna manera, podría servir como referencia para la Hormiga González si consigue destacar en Grecia. Por su parte, Alan Pulido permaneció dos años en el Olympiacos y, a diferencia de Castillo, terminó regresando a la Liga MX, donde posteriormente defendió nuevamente la camiseta de Chivas. Ahora habrá que esperar qué sucede con la Hormiga. En México existe la ilusión de que el delantero pueda trascender en Europa, pero el mexicano tendrá que responder dentro de la cancha. Y es que llega al Olympiacos después de acumular 12 partidos entre Chivas y la Selección Mexicana sin marcar gol, por lo que su adaptación y sus primeros minutos en Grecia serán claves para comenzar a cambiar esa historia.

articles.title: SEC Adopts Rule Change Banning NFL, NBA, WNBA Players From Returning, Penalties Reportedly Revealed
articles.summary: The SEC announced Tuesday that teams are prohibited from rostering players who have either declared for the NFL, NBA or WNBA drafts and did not withdraw within the allowed framework, signed a contract with a team in those leagues or were at any point rostered by a team in one of those leagues.
articles.body:
The SEC announced Tuesday that teams are prohibited from rostering players who have either declared for the NFL, NBA or WNBA drafts and did not withdraw within the allowed framework, signed a contract with a team in those leagues or were at any point rostered by a team in one of those leagues.

That comes after tight end Dae'Quan Wright had an agreement in place with LSU to play for the football team after signing contracts with the Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns this offseason.

Earlier on Tuesday, the Big Ten instituted a similar rule.

"The Big Ten Conference announced Tuesday the unanimous adoption of a conference rule to prohibit football players who have signed a professional contract, were on a professional roster at any point or declared for the NFL Draft as an underclassman without withdrawing, from maintaining eligibility for athletic competition at a conference institution," the conference announced in a statement . "The conference continues to evaluate potential rules restricting professional athletes in other sports from conference competition."

Notre Dame, an independent, is reportedly taking that stance as well.

And the Big 12 is also reportedly leaning heavily in that direction:

The ACC is set to discuss the matter this week.

Both Wright and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Zxavian Harris agreed to join LSU this offseason after a temporary restraining order was granted by a Louisiana judge allowing them a fifth year of eligibility. This offseason the NCAA ruled that athletes could have five years of eligibility in five consecutive seasons but didn't grandfather in the rule for athletes who first played in the 2022-23 academic year. A number of athletes in various states have sued, seeking that fifth year.

Both Wright and Harris previously played under LSU head coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss.

articles.title: La remontada más bestia para jugar la Champions: el LASK se carga al Celtic en una noche memorable
articles.standfirst: El Bodo y el Shabab, los otros dos clasificados del martes
articles.summary: El Bodo y el Shabab, los otros dos clasificados del martes
articles.body: El Bodo/Glimt, revelación de la pasada Champions, confirmó su regreso a la máxima competición continental junto al Sabah y el LASK, que hicieron historia en sendas eliminatorias increíbles que se fueron a la prórroga. La del LASK, equipo austríaco, superó todos los niveles y consumó la debacle del Celtic, con muchas más horas de vuelo. Martes 25 de agosto:  Bodo/Glimt 3-0 (6-1) NEC Nimega     Sabah 5-2 (6-4) Hapoel Be'er Sheva LASK 5-1 (5-4) Celtic Miércoles 26 de agosto:  Lyon 21.00 (1-1) Fenerbahce AEK Atenas 21.00 (0-0) Levski Sofía Viking 21.00 (2-2) Dinamo Zagreb Celje 21.00 (1-1) Slovan Bratislava El Sabah de Azerbaiyán, club fundado hace sólo nueve años, acabó con el Hapoel Be'er Sheva (5-2) después de levantar el 2-1 que traían del primer asalto. Un gol de Mutallimov en el minuto 94 forzó la prórroga y, allí, los tantos de Mbina y Mickels pusieron la rúbrica a una clasificación histórica. Mucho más allá fue el LASK, capaz de cargarse en el partido de vuelta de la previa al Celtic, que sentía tener el billete en el bolsillo cuando salió de Glasgow. Y bien abrochado. Los católicos venían de ganar 3-0 en la ida e incluso abrieron el marcador en una noche que jamás se olvidará en Linz y que pasa a la historia de las rondas previas de la Liga de Campeones.  El equipo austríaco, cuatro goles abajo, igualó la eliminatoria en el minuto 90 por medio de Flecker y ajustició al Celtic en la prórroga con un gol de Adeniran en el 109' (5-1). El LASK, que hasta tuvo tiempo de fallar un penalti en el último suspiro, vuelve a la Champions, territorio que no pisaba desde la lejanísima Copa de Europa de 1965. Por su parte, el que no falló como el Celtic fue el Bodo, que venía de ganar 1-3 al NEC Nimega y le metió otros tres en el partido de vuelta. Los noruegos vuelven a estar preparados para sorprender a Europa. Este miércoles, se conocerán los últimos cuatro equipos que jugarán la fase liga de la Champions. El Lyon-Fenerbahce centra toda la atención. Uno de los dos, equipos de peso, faltará en el sorteo del jueves en Mónaco, en el que tenemos cinco equipos españoles (Barcelona, Real Madrid, Atlético, Villarreal y Betis).

articles.title: Jonas Urbig still has fondness for FC Köln, but Bayern Munich was perfect next step
articles.summary: Jonas Urbig cannot say enough about FC Bayern’s club environment.
articles.body:
After spending more than a decade at FC Köln, Jonas Urbig knew that moving to Bayern Munich would be a major change. But according to the young goalkeeper, settling in at his new club happened much faster than he expected.

Speaking to Bayern Munich's club magazine Säbener51, Urbig opened up about leaving Köln and discovering what life is really like inside Bayern Munich:

"I will always have an emotional connection with Köln. I wish the club nothing but the best – unless they are playing against us. At first, I only knew Bayern Munich from the outside. But once I got to know the club from within, I quickly realized how human and open everyone at the club is. From the outside, 'Mia San Mia' can often sound like just a slogan, but today I know that it is genuinely lived here. And that feels really good. That was certainly one of the reasons why I felt very quickly that I was in the right place here," Urbig said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

Urbig's comments offer an interesting perspective on the culture at Bayern Munich. From the outside, "Mia San Mia" can easily be viewed as nothing more than a famous club motto. For Urbig, however, experiencing the environment firsthand has given the phrase an entirely different meaning.

After more than ten years in Köln, leaving a club that played such an important role in his development could never be easy. But Urbig appears to have found a new home in Munich, surrounded by a group that has made him feel welcome from the beginning.

Now, his goal is to continue developing and prove that he belongs at Bayern Munich.

articles.title: LASK v Celtic: Martin O'Neill takes responsibility
articles.summary: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill says his team have a "million miles to go" after defeat in Austria.
articles.body:
In the open air of the Raiffeisen Arena, with bedlam all around, there was nowhere to hide for Celtic or Martin O'Neill.

The Scottish champions had endured one of the darkest nights in their European history.

After going out to Kairat Almaty on penalties last year at this stage of the Champions League play-offs, that is saying something.

Four goals up on aggregate against LASK, O'Neill's Celtic somehow conspired to implode in a second half with little sign of a response on the way to a 5-4 aggregate loss following extra time.

There was no hiding place, and the Celtic manager was frank when put in the spotlight at full-time.

"I'm responsible for this one," he said.

"Without a doubt. Naturally it took me a long time to get over the Uefa Cup final in 2003 but this was majorly disappointing.

"In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through.

"We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That's absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway."

Celtic blow four-goal lead to LASK in Champions League collapse

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded Published 4 hours ago

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded

O'Neill was not in charge for that defeat in Kazakhstan a year ago as it triggered the start of the end for Brendan Rodgers' second spell at Celtic Park.

The current Parkhead boss helped steady Celtic's ship last term following Rodgers' exit and again following the Wilfried Nancy saga to guide them to another league title and a Scottish Cup.

This season appeared to get off to a prosperous start until the roof began to cave in over in Austria.

Away from the raw pain of stumbling in such a stark way, the aftermath could be telling for Celtic who now have to not only pick themselves up, but finish off a transfer window without the hefty windfall which would have blown in with the Champions League.

"The qualification for the Champions League is major, it's major in every aspect," said O'Neill.

"Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That's my responsibility again to do that.

"I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis.

"That's not going to be the case but we'll see. Tonight we came up well and truly short, particularly in the second half."

Celtic captain Callum McGregor tells Amazon Prime: "We got what we deserved. We were passive all night. We looked scared to go and win the game.

"I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and got away with it.

"We have to suck it up. We apologise to our supporters and the club because there's no way we should lose that game.

"It's as much on the players as everyone else. You can't look for excuses elsewhere.

"You'll now see what people are made of. When you play like that you can't have any excuses whatsoever.

"When you go 1-0 up in the game and it still doesn't settle you, you can't have any excuse and that's on us.

"You fall at a big hurdle and these questions [on whether the squad are ready] are going to be asked. You can't lose by that margin then look for excuses elsewhere.

"This is what it's like to play at Celtic. You have to bounce back, you have to show a reaction and that's what Celtic are all about."

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown on BBC Radio Scotland: " It was a fantastic start, you go 1-0 up, but that seems like forever ago. Now they've crashed out the Champions League and conceded five goals.

"LASK outran Celtic in a couple of areas, the two up front were strong, solid and willing runners.

"LASK deserve to go through with that performance. I feel for the lads because I've been in that situation as well."

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Amazon Prime: "It looked to me as if Celtic were exhausted. Fragile in duels. It only looked like there would be one winner.

"They battered Celtic tonight, physically and on the football side. It could have been more."

Former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov: "Everyone [is to blame].

"They are all in it together. A big club like Celtic should be able to hold that out."

articles.title: Big Ten, SEC approve ban on pro players returning to college to play; ACC, Big 12 considering move
articles.summary: The SEC announced Monday night that professionals should not "return to college competition."
articles.body:
With the Big Ten making the first move, the ACC and Big 12 are now also considering a ban on former professional players who want to return to play in college, according to Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger .

The Big Ten formally adopted that policy on Tuesday, officially making underclassmen who declared for the NFL Draft and didn't withdraw, signed pro contracts or appeared on an NFL roster ineligible. The Big Ten's vote was unanimous.

"The conference continues to evaluate potential rules restricting professional athletes in other sports from conference competition," the league said in a statement, in part.

The Big Ten later announced the penalties for violating the rule: a coach suspension of 50% of the season and an institutional fine .

Then on Tuesday afternoon, the SEC followed suit. The conference announced a similar policy for both football and basketball. The Big Ten's move only included football.

Notre Dame officials have told the Big Ten and SEC that it the school will also follow a similar policy.

The flurry of discussions comes after the reports that Dae'Quan Wright of the Cleveland Browns and Zxavian Harris of the New Orleans Saints are leaving their respective NFL teams to play for LSU . Both Wright and Harris played for Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss.

Kiffin defended courting pro players on Monday during a press conference while being careful not to confirm any new signings, saying, "[They're] either going to play for you or they're going to play for someone else around the country."

On Monday, SEC presidents met virtually to support opposition to professional players coming back to play in college.

"College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference. Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition," read part of the SEC's statement.

With Tuesday's decision, SEC schools are no longer allowed to have such athletes on their rosters for football or basketball. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey was granted "full and unlimited authority," which includes suspending a school from competition, according to Dellenger .

More discussions are expected Tuesday during a joint, two-day meeting of SEC presidents and athletic directors in Birmingham, Alabama — an unusual and significant gathering that was previously scheduled.

With the conferences all considering a ban, and the Big Ten's move to adopt such a policy, it could open them up to additional legal action and may put the leagues themselves at the center of new lawsuits — instead of the NCAA.

Additionally, if the conferences agree on a ban, they'd also need to determine the penalties for playing an ineligible player.

Whether the ACC and Big 12 follow the Big Ten's lead now remains to be seen.

articles.title: Champions League 26/27 draw, dates, schedule, format and who has qualified from Premier League and around Europe
articles.summary: Arsenal, Man Utd , Liverpool, Man City and Aston Villa will all take part in the 2026/27 Champions League; draw for the league phase will take place in Monaco on Thursday
articles.body:
A total of 36 teams will enter the competition at this stage after 29 qualified at the end of last season. The remaining seven places are determined by the qualifiers.

In the new format, which is entering its third season since being implemented, teams now play fixtures against eight different teams - two teams from Pots 1, 2, 3 and 4.

Half of the eight league-phase matches are at home, with the other half away.

The draw is done by a supercomputer, which automatically selects the eight opponents by one touch of a button.

While four places via qualifiers are yet to be determined, 32 teams have been confirmed.

The pots are allocated based on UEFA's club coefficient rankings, which reflects results in European competitions across a five-year period ending in 2025/26.

Back-to-back champions Paris Saint-Germain , Bayern Munich , Real Madrid , Liverpool , Manchester City , Inter Milan, Arsenal, Barcelona and Atletico Madrid are in Pot 1.

Manchester United and Europa League winners Aston Villa , two clubs making their return to Europe's elite competition, have been placed in Pot 2.

The top eight sides in the league will qualify automatically for the round of 16, while teams finishing 25th or lower are eliminated and do not drop into the Europa League.

The teams finishing in ninth to 24th place compete in a two-legged knockout-phase play-off. Teams finishing between ninth and 16th are seeded, meaning they will face a team in 17th-24th with the return leg at home.

The eight clubs who win their knockout-phase play-off each meet one of the seeded top-eight finishers in the league-phase table for a place in the quarter-finals.
